title: European Club Cup: Three co-leaders in both sections going into final round
summary:
Three teams share the lead in both sections of the European Club Cup ahead of Friday's final round. In the open, SuperChess and Novy Bor drew their direct encounter, allowing Bayegan Pendik to catch up with a narrow victory over Tuxera Aquaprofit Nagykanizsai. In the women's competition, Gambit Bonnevoie suffered their first defeat, leaving Monte-Carlo and Odlar Yurdu level with the Luxembourg club. | Pictured: Bayegan Pendik's Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus | Photo: Gerd Densing

Open: Contested matches at the top

Three teams share first place in the open section of the European Club Cup following Thursday's sixth (and penultimate) round in Budva.

Defending champions SuperChess Romania and Novy Bor Chess Club drew their direct encounter 3–3, allowing top seeds Bayegan Pendik Chess Sports Club to catch them with a narrow 3½–2½ victory over Tuxera Aquaprofit Nagykanizsai.

All three teams enter the final round with 11/12 match points, while four clubs remain in contention for medals with 10 points.

Sveti Stefan, a small island connected to the mainland by a narrow tombolo, is situated approximately 6 kilometres (3.7 mi) southeast of Budva - Bobby Fischer and Boriss Spassky played the first 11 games of their 1992 rematch on the island | Photo: Gerd Densing

The encounter between SuperChess and Novy Bor featured four decisive games, with both teams holding the advantage at different stages. On the top board, Nodirbek Abdusattorov defeated his namesake and teammate Nodirbek Yakubboev to give the Romanian club an important point. Nihal Sarin responded by beating Jorden van Foreest on board two.

Bogdan-Daniel Deac subsequently put SuperChess ahead by defeating Nils Grandelius, while David Navara overcame Daniel Dardha on the sixth board to restore equality. Notably, Dardha came from winning all five of his previous games in Budva. The remaining two encounters ended drawn.

Novy Bor v. SuperChess | Photo: Gerd Densing

SuperChess 3-3 Novy Bor

Select an entry from the list to switch between games

While the top match saw the co-leaders split the match points, Bayegan Pendik secured a crucial victory over fifth seeds Tuxera Aquaprofit Nagykanizsai. The Turkish representatives overcame an individual defeat on the top board, where Indian grandmaster Pranesh M defeated Anish Giri. It was Giri's second loss in four appearances at the tournament.

Victories by Amin Tabatabaei against Andrei Volokitin and Volodar Murzin against Maksim Chigaev proved sufficient for Bayegan Pendik to win the match.

Anish Giri and Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus playing on the top two boards for Bayegan Pendik | Photo: Gerd Densing

Tuxera Aquaprofit Nagykanizsai 2½-3½ Bayegan Pendik

Elektroprivreda, the sixth seeds, missed an opportunity to join the leaders after being held to a 3–3 draw by second seeds Alkaloid. Elektroprivreda, representing Montenegro, nevertheless remain just one match point behind the leading trio. They are joined on 10/12 by Rishon LeZion A, Marseille Echecs and Cheddleton Savills Caterling.

Friday's final round will see Bayegan Pendik face SuperChess in a direct encounter between two of the leaders, while Novy Bor take on Elektroprivreda. Cheddleton will meet Rishon LeZion A, while Marseille Echecs face Alkaloid.

Arjun Erigaisi, Wei Yi (not in the photo) and Yu Yangyi lead Alkaloid, the second seeds in Budva | Photo: Gerd Densing

Women's: Gambit Bonnevoie suffer first loss

The women's competition also has three teams tied for first place ahead of Friday's final round. CE Gambit Bonnevoie, who had won all five of their previous matches, suffered their first defeat against fifth seeds Odlar Yurdu, while defending champions Cercle d'Echecs de Monte-Carlo narrowly defeated SuperChess Romania.

The results leave all three teams on 10/12 match points, with Sirmium Sremska Mitrovica, Crvena Zvezda and Davit Jojua's Chess Club following on 8/12. Since none of the co-leaders face each other (they have already played each other in previous rounds), the three chasers have a very small theoretical chance of creating a six-way tie at the top if all three score wins.

The penultimate round in progress | Photo: Gerd Densing

Gambit Bonnevoie entered the sixth round with a two-point advantage over their closest pursuers, having already defeated the three highest-rated teams in the competition. However, the Luxembourg-based club could not extend their winning streak against Azerbaijan's Odlar Yurdu, who secured a 2½–1½ victory.

The decisive point came on the fourth board, where Khanim Balajayeva defeated Aleksandra Maltsevskaya. The remaining three games ended in draws. The victory allowed Odlar Yurdu to catch their opponents in the standings.

Anna Ushenina facing Ulviyya Fataliyeva on the top board | Photo: Gerd Densing

Gambit Bonnevoie 1½-2½ Odlar Yurdu

Monte-Carlo joined the leading group by defeating third seeds SuperChess Romania 2½–1½. Stavroula Tsolakidou scored the only victory of the match, beating Deimante Daulyte-Cornette on board three.

The encounter was particularly demanding for Monte-Carlo on the remaining boards. Cramling managed to save a difficult position against Marsel Efroimski, while Humpy Koneru defended a pawn-down endgame against Dinara Wagner in a 95-move game. Koneru finally secured the half-point that gave her team the match victory.

Monte-Carlo's Aleksandra Goryachkina and Humpy Koneru | Photo: Gerd Densing

Monte-Carlo 2½-1½ SuperChess

Elsewhere, 11-year-old English star Bodhana Sivanandan recorded her fourth individual win in Budva, defeating Arina Budiak of Klaipeda. Representing She Plays To Win Lionesses A, Sivanandan has collected 4½/6 points, with her only defeat coming against Aleksandra Goryachkina (the highest-rated player in the field) in the opening round.

The final round will see Monte-Carlo face 15 th seeds Davit Jojua's Chess Club, while Odlar Yurdu take on second seeds Sirmium Sremska Mitrovica. Gambit Bonnevoie will meet seventh seeds Crvena Zvezda. As mentioned above, none of the three leaders will face each other.

additionalSources.title: Leaders Caught As 3 Teams Tie For Top Before Euro Club Cup Final Round
additionalSources.summary: Leaders SuperChess Romania and Novy Bor Chess Club fought out a thrilling draw in round six of the 2026 European Chess Club Cup, with wins for GMs Nodirbek Abdusattorov and Bogdan-Daniel Deac balanced out by wins for GMs Nihal Sarin and David Navara. That enabled top-seed Bayegan Pendik Chess Sports Club to rejoin them in the lead before the final round, after a nerve-wracking 3.5-2.5 win over Tuxera Aquaprofit Nagykanizsai. GMs Amin Tabatabaei and Volodar Murzin more than made up for GM Anish Giri losing on top board to GM Pranesh M. We also have a trio of leaders in the 2026 European Women's Chess Club Cup after fourth-seed CE Gambit Bonnevoie, which had beaten the first, second, and third seeds, finally fell to the fifth—Odlar Yurdu. The match was decided by a single win, for IM Khanim Balajayeva over IM Aleksandra Maltsevskaya, while they were caught by defending champion Cercle d'Echecs de Monte-Carlo, which also relied on a single win—IM Stavroula Tsolakidou's defeat of IM Deimante Daulyte-Cornette. The final round is on Friday, October 23, starting at 8 a.m. ET / 14:00 CEST / 5:30 p.m. IST. There were four wins as the last two remaining perfect teams fought out a 3-3 tie at the top, enabling the Turkish top seed to catch them with a narrow win. Two of the leaders, SuperChess Romania and Bayegan Pendik Chess Sports Club, face off in the final round, while Novy Bor takes on Elektroprivreda, a single point back. Cheddleton, Marseille, and Rishon can also sneak onto the podium with a win, though their tiebreaks likely make gold an impossibility. Open Standings After Round 6 (Top 12) The penultimate round was all we could have hoped for, with incredibly tense battles in the top matches. That was summed up by the battle on top board between the two teams on a perfect 10/10 score. As Abdusattorov described it: "I played against my good friend, my namemate [GM] Nodirbek Yakubboev." Abdusattorov said it was "annoying" to have to play a friend, but on the board neither player held back as Abdusattorov unleashed some sharp home preparation with 11.g4 and Yakubboev responded in kind. The word that Abdusattorov kept returning to was "complicated," but in the end he managed to punish a final mistake and clinch an important win.

title: Wesley So Wins 4th U.S. Chess Championship
summary: GM Wesley So won his fourth national title at the 2026 U.S. Chess Championship after beating the defending champion, GM Fabiano Caruana, 1.5-0.5 in rapid tiebreaks. The previous day played out the least likely scenario: So lost to GM Sam Sevian and Caruana won on demand in his game just to make it to the playoffs. But after a nearly sleepless night, So came back to win his first U.S. Championship in four years and $56,000. As covered in the previous report, WIM Rachael Li won the 2026 U.S. Women's Chess Championship in round 11 without any playoffs. The next world-class event at the Saint Louis Chess Club is the 2026 Clutch Chess Champions Showdown featuring the blockbuster lineup of GMs Javokhir Sindarov, Caruana, Hikaru Nakamura, and Praggnanandhaa Rameshbabu. The three-day event begins on Tuesday, October 27, at 1 p.m. ET / 19:00 CEST / 10:30 p.m. IST. Final Standings | Open So won his first title in 2017, then won again in 2020 and 2021, and four years later he's earned his fourth. This year must be one of the toughest, considering the catastrophe in round 11, but he nevertheless maintained that 2017 was the most difficult as it fielded a 2817-rated Caruana and a 2793-rated Nakamura, as well as a dangerous GM Alex Onischuk, who also played at a 2800+ level in that event as well, according to So. After the last-round loss against Sevian, So said, "I didn't sleep well at all... only two or three hours." Hardly able to put the loss behind him, he was not in the mood to play, but So also gave credit where credit is due. "Kudos to Sam. He had a very tough tournament. I was shocked with the way he played a really good game, but I also played very badly." Kudos to Sam. He had a very tough tournament. —Wesley So on Sam Sevian So commented that this year's championship featured an unusual amount of blunders. He said he was losing against GMs Ray Robson and Jeffery Xiong, but ended up winning both games. The level of play with Caruana in the playoffs was also "very poor quality for both of us. So many blunders and so many mistakes." Both players had just played at the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Uzbekistan before this event, and he said, "In the end, I was really on my last breath. I was literally seeing 10 pawns for Black; my mind was all over the place. But I think Fabi was extremely tired too." It's hard to say who was the moral winner in the draw in game one. So gained a winning advantage with the black pieces in a Nimzo-Indian Defense and could have won on the spot if he had found 34...Qd4+ and 35...Ra1, not a hard combination to spot under normal circumstances—if we may ignore exhaustion and nerves. Caruana went on to save a dead-lost, pawn-down endgame.
